cards.name: Actions
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Actions panel, which stores recorded sequences of Photoshop steps in sets and plays them back on the active document, or on a whole folder of files through File > Automate > Batch. Like the other Window menu panel entries it is a toggle: choosing it while the panel is showing hides it. In the harvest the Layers tab it was grouped with did not come back to the front after the second run.
cards.how: Create a set, click New Action, press Record, perform the steps, then Stop. Play runs the selected action on the active document. Insert Menu Item records commands that do not record on their own, Insert Stop adds a pause with a message, and the dialog toggle beside a step makes it stop for input. Button Mode in the panel menu turns actions into one-click buttons; File > Automate > Batch or Create Droplet runs an action over a folder.
use_for: repeating the same resize, sharpen and export steps on a set of product photos
batch-processing a folder of images into web-sized JPEGs through File > Automate > Batch
giving a script a recorded step to replay with app.doAction when the step has no DOM call
avoid: steps that depend on what is in each image (subject position, text length): actions replay blindly, use a script with logic instead
freehand painting: brush strokes only record with Allow Tool Recording on and replay at fixed coordinates, so paint by hand or generate the texture
cards.script_api: app.runMenuItem(stringIDToTypeID('toggleActionsPalette')) (verified live 2026-10-04: the Actions panel appeared). To play an action without the panel (unverified): app.doAction('Action Name', 'Set Name').

review.changes: none

cards.name: Adjustments
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Adjustments panel, whose buttons add a non-destructive adjustment layer (Brightness/Contrast, Levels, Curves, Exposure, Vibrance, Hue/Saturation, Color Balance, Black & White, Photo Filter, Channel Mixer, Color Lookup, Invert, Posterize, Threshold, Gradient Map, Selective Color) above the active layer, and whose Adjustment Presets section applies ready-made looks in one click; the settings then open in the Properties panel. Like the other Window menu panel entries it is a toggle: choosing it while the panel is showing hides it.
cards.how: Select the layer to correct, click an adjustment icon or a preset thumbnail (hovering a preset previews it on the canvas) and tune it in Properties. The adjustment changes every layer below it; clip it (the clip button in Properties, or Layer > Create Clipping Mask) to limit it to the layer directly below, and paint its mask black to hide it in areas.
use_for: colour-grading a poster photo with Curves and Hue/Saturation that stay editable
matching the tone of a product cut-out to its background with a clipped adjustment
one-click cinematic or black-and-white looks for social posts from Adjustment Presets
avoid: a correction that must be baked into the pixels for another app: merge it down, or apply Image > Adjustments directly to a pixel layer

Shadows/Highlights: it is not an adjustment layer; apply it to a smart object as a Smart Filter instead (HDR Toning is not an adjustment layer either and cannot be a Smart Filter: it works on a flattened image)
cards.script_api: app.runMenuItem(stringIDToTypeID('toggleCreatePanel')) (verified live 2026-10-04: the Adjustments panel appeared). To add an adjustment layer without the panel (unverified): executeAction(stringIDToTypeID('make'), desc, DialogModes.NO) with null = reference to class adjustmentLayer and using = an adjustmentLayer descriptor whose type holds e.g. a levels or curves descriptor.

review.changes: avoid: said HDR Toning can be applied as a Smart Filter (it cannot; it flattens the image); how: replaced the unharvested Alt-click gesture with the clip button / Layer > Create Clipping Mask

use_for: cutting out hair or foliage by turning the highest-contrast channel into a mask
storing complex selections as alpha channels to reuse later in the file
adding a spot colour plate (Pantone or white ink) for packaging print
avoid: editing a colour channel directly on the only copy of an image: it is destructive; use a Channel Mixer or Curves adjustment layer
keeping alpha channels in a JPEG or PNG export: they are dropped; save as PSD or TIFF

cards.name: Character
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Character panel, which sets type formatting for the selected type layer or highlighted text: font family and style, size, leading, kerning, tracking, vertical and horizontal scale, baseline shift, colour, faux bold / italic, caps, super- and subscript, underline, strikethrough, OpenType features, language and anti-aliasing. Same command as Type > Panels > Character Panel. Like the other Window menu panel entries it is a toggle: choosing it while the panel is showing hides it.
cards.how: Select a type layer to format all of it, or highlight characters with the Type tool to format only those, then change the values; tracking spaces a whole run of letters, kerning sets the gap between the two letters at the text cursor.
use_for: setting headline tracking and leading for a poster or thumbnail title
styling prices, units and superscripts in product promos
switching on ligatures and stylistic alternates for logotype text
avoid: alignment, indents and hyphenation: use the Paragraph panel
giving many text layers the same look: save a Character Style instead of retyping values
cards.script_api: app.runMenuItem(stringIDToTypeID('toggleCharacterPalette')) (verified live 2026-10-04: the panel appeared and a second run hid it). Formatting by script (unverified): artLayer.textItem.font, .size, .tracking, .leading and .color on a text layer.

review.changes: how: removed the unharvested Alt+Left / Right arrow shortcut

cards.name: Character Styles
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Character Styles panel, which keeps named sets of character formatting (font, size, colour, tracking and so on) that can be applied to selected text in one click; editing a style updates all text that uses it, and a + after a style name marks local overrides. Same command as Type > Panels > Character Styles Panel. Like the other Window menu panel entries it is a toggle: choosing it while the panel is showing hides it.
cards.how: Format some text, then create a new style from the panel (it takes its formatting from the selected text) and double-click it to edit its options. Click a style to apply it to the selected type; Clear Override removes local formatting and Redefine Style updates the style from the selection. Load Character Styles in the panel menu imports styles from another PSD.
use_for: consistent price, label and caption styling across a multi-artboard social campaign
restyling every highlighted word in a set of thumbnails by editing one style
sharing a brand's type styles between template PSDs
avoid: one-off formatting of a single headline: use the Character panel
text that will be edited in another app: the styles stay in the PSD; Illustrator needs its own
cards.script_api: app.runMenuItem(stringIDToTypeID('toggleCharacterStylesPalette')) (verified live 2026-10-04: the panel appeared and a second run hid it). The DOM has no character style API; set the formatting directly through artLayer.textItem properties instead (unverified).

review.changes: none

cards.name: Clone Source
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Clone Source panel, which holds several clone-source slots for the Clone Stamp and Healing Brush tools and transforms the sampled pixels: X / Y offset, width and height scale, rotation and flip, plus an overlay preview (opacity, blend mode, clipped, auto hide) and a frame offset for video layers. Like the other Window menu panel entries it is a toggle: choosing it while the panel is showing hides it.
cards.how: Sample a source point with Clone Stamp or Healing Brush to set the source in the selected slot. Set Scale or Angle to clone at another size or rotation, use flip for mirrored repairs, and turn on Show Overlay to see the source under the brush before painting.
use_for: retouching product shots by cloning a texture at another scale or angle
mirroring one side of a symmetrical object to repair the other
restoring damaged old photos while previewing the source overlay
avoid: removing large objects: Content-Aware Fill or the Remove tool is faster than manual cloning
scripted retouching: cloning needs hand-placed strokes; Edit > Fill with Content-Aware on a selection can be scripted

cards.name: Color
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Color panel, which shows the foreground and background colours and lets you set them with sliders (Grayscale, RGB, HSB, CMYK, Lab, Web Color) or a colour ramp, cube or wheel, with a warning when a colour is outside the CMYK print gamut. Like the other Window menu panel entries it is a toggle: choosing it while the panel is showing hides it. The harvest's run hid the panel, which was already open.
cards.how: Click the foreground or background swatch in the panel, then drag the sliders or click in the spectrum. The panel menu switches slider modes and the ramp / cube / wheel view; clicking the gamut warning swaps in the nearest printable colour.
use_for: setting brand colours by exact RGB or CMYK values for text and shapes
picking accent colours on the colour wheel for a poster palette
checking that a vivid colour will print within the CMYK gamut
avoid: storing reusable brand colours: save them in the Swatches panel
taking a colour from the image: use the Eyedropper tool

cards.name: Comments
cards.summary: Shows or hides the Comments panel, used with Photoshop cloud documents that are shared for review or editing: it lists collaborators' comments, pinned to a point or area on the canvas, and lets you reply, resolve and filter them. Ordinary local PSD files have no such comments, so the panel stays empty for them. Like the other Window menu panel entries it is a toggle: choosing it while the panel is showing hides it.
cards.how: Save the file as a cloud document and share it (invite people or share a review link); their comments then appear in the panel. Click a comment to jump to its pin, reply, or mark it resolved.
use_for: collecting client feedback pinned to exact spots on a poster or social post
tracking which revision notes on a campaign visual have been resolved
avoid: local files and offline work: comments need a cloud document; leave notes in a PSD with the Notes panel instead
automated pipelines: there is no script route for comments
